claims.text: The proposed intervention is an active-learning machine-learning interatomic potential continuously retrained on ab initio configurations from both solid and liquid phases.
The active-learning potential will significantly improve reference–target phase-space overlap relative to conventional EAM references.
The active-learning potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The intervention is applicable to solid and liquid CoCrFeMnNi or AlCoFeNi at or near their melting temperatures.
The applicable composition range consists of high-entropy alloys containing five or more metallic elements.
The intervention applies to both superheated liquids and high-temperature solids.
The target HEAs exhibit diverse local atomic environments and high-temperature short-range order.
A flexible, continuously updated ML potential can capture this diversity of local environments and short-range order.
Conventional fixed EAM references inadequately represent the many configurations of the ab initio HEA liquid.
Sampling and learning from new configurations during simulation reduces the configuration-space gap between the reference and ab initio target systems.
Improved phase-space overlap shortens the effective thermodynamic-integration path.
Shortening the effective integration path lowers thermodynamic-integration mismatch error.
The intervention is expected to reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 30–50% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The reduced path mismatch will produce more accurate free-energy predictions.
The advantage of active learning may diminish in simpler systems or at temperatures far from melting because configurational diversity is less pronounced there.
Failure to achieve at least an approximately 30% mismatch reduction, or failure to improve phase-space-overlap metrics significantly, is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: AlCoFeNi is supplied as an applicable example even though it contains four named elements, while the conditions and boundary restrict the intervention to alloys with five or more elements.
